name: Kevin Guo
current_role: Chairman & President, Yunnan Botanee Bio-Technology Group (SZSE: 300957), parent of Winona skincare (if Kevin Guo = Guo Zhenyu)
profile: Botanee wealth on Hurun lists belongs to founder-chairman Guo Zhenyu (郭振宇), a former engineering/biomedical academic who returned to China in 2003 to run Dihon Pharmaceutical, then built Botanee around Winona, China's leading sensitive-skin skincare brand. Botanee listed in Shenzhen in March 2021; he is now expanding brands like Winona Baby and Aoxmed.
interesting_fact: Winona started as a medical-skincare brand incubated inside Dihon Pharmaceutical around 2008; Botanee was originally just Winona's distributor before becoming its parent and listing in Shenzhen in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Guo Zhenyu earned a PhD in electrical engineering, moved into biomedical engineering, and became a tenured professor at George Washington University in 2002 before giving it up to return to China in 2003 as chairman of Dihon Pharmaceutical, where he built the OTC dermatology brand Kangwang (康王).
notes: Identity ambiguous: input mixes Botanee (Guo Zhenyu) with 'Hurun Unicorn founders' listings, which may instead refer to Kevin Guo, co-founder/CEO of US AI unicorn Hive. Profile above is for Guo Zhenyu. Botanee IR handled by board secretary Wang Long; no published IR email found (company says it answers investor emails and SZSE Hudongyi questions).

name: Zheng Bei
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Executive Vice President, Pharmaron Beijing (SZSE: 300759; HKEX: 3759)
profile: Zheng Bei (郑北) co-founded Pharmaron, a Beijing-based contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRO/CDMO), in 2004 with Boliang Lou and Larry Lou. She set up its administration, HR and accounting functions and leads its capacity build-out; her wealth comes from her Pharmaron stake, held jointly with Lou Xiaoqiang per Hurun.
interesting_fact: Pharmaron grew from a 2004 Beijing start-up into a global CRO/CDMO with sites in China, the US and the UK, listed in both Shenzhen (2019) and Hong Kong (2019).
deep_cut_fact: She personally led Pharmaron's capacity expansion across China, building more than 10 R&D and manufacturing sites totalling over 10 million square feet; she holds bachelor's and master's degrees in management and administration from Peking University.

public_contacts.value: ellen.cabral@pharmaron.com (media contact on Pharmaron press releases)

notes: Low public profile; operational executive rather than spokesperson. Best route is Pharmaron corporate communications.

name: Tsai Chi-jui
current_role: Co-founder and long-time group president (總裁) of Pou Chen Group, Taichung, Taiwan; daughter Tsai Pei-chun has been CEO since 2012
profile: Tsai Chi-jui (蔡其瑞) co-founded Pou Chen with his brothers in 1969, starting with rubber shoes and slipper processing; it became the world's largest branded athletic/casual footwear maker, producing 200M+ pairs a year for Nike, Adidas, Asics and New Balance (incl. via HK-listed Yue Yuen). Now in his 80s, he has largely handed operations to the next generation.
interesting_fact: Before footwear he was a primary-school fine-arts teacher; Business Today credited his artistic eye for Pou Chen's distinctive shoe-upper designs that won over sneaker brands, and noted Pou Chen made Nike's Air Jordan line.
deep_cut_fact: A Lukang native and Taichung Normal College graduate, classmates recalled he had a fine singing voice and single-handedly did every class art contest and wall poster; he reluctantly left teaching and opened a shoe-upper/slipper factory in 1969 with NT$150,000. In 2014 he was still wearing his trademark Nike sneakers with shirt and slacks.
notes: Described by Forbes as humble and intensely private; born c.1940 (68 in 2008). No recent public statements found; route via Pou Chen spokesperson's office. Alive status assumed from continued 2025-26 rich-list appearances; no death reports found.

name: Hugo Ribeiro
current_role: Controlling shareholder, Amaggi (Brazilian agribusiness group), alongside Blairo Maggi and Itamar Locks
profile: Hugo Ribeiro is the son-in-law of Lucia Maggi, who co-founded Amaggi with her late husband André Maggi. Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest soybean and grain producers and traders (farming, logistics, energy); Ribeiro is one of its controlling family shareholders with Blairo Maggi and Itamar Locks. He keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Ribeiro previously served as president of the board of an Amaggi-linked research institute dedicated to developing more sustainable soybean varieties (per Forbes).
notes: Very private; almost no press coverage under his own name. Amaggi also generates hydropower in Mato Grosso, a possible energy angle. Best route is Amaggi's communications office.

name: Mehmet Omer Koc
current_role: Chairman, Koç Holding (since Feb 2016); also chairs Tüpraş and Koç University's board of trustees
profile: Mehmet Ömer Koç (b. 1962, Ankara), second son of Rahmi Koç, is third-generation leader of Turkey's largest conglomerate, Koç Holding (energy/refining via Tüpraş, autos, appliances via Arçelik/Beko, banking). He joined the group in 1992, led its Energy Group, became vice chairman in 2008 and chairman in 2016 after his brother Mustafa's death.
interesting_fact: A major art patron, he founded the Istanbul contemporary art space Arter in 2010, sponsors the Istanbul Biennial and Turkey's Venice Biennale pavilion, and is reputed to hold one of the finest private collections of Ottoman objects and books; he also sits on the Bilderberg steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: Before his MBA at Columbia Business School (1989), he earned a BA in Ancient Greek from Columbia College (1985), and began his career at Kofisa Trading in Geneva before joining Koç Holding as a finance coordinator in 1992.

public_contacts.value: https://www.koc.com.tr/investor-relations (Koç Holding Investor Relations; contact via IR menu)

notes: Known for avoiding media; lives largely in London. Strong energy angle via Tüpraş (Turkey's largest refiner) and the group's former Energy Group, which he led. Route via Koç Holding corporate communications. Not to be confused with a younger Mehmet Ömer Koç on the board of Bilkom.
